title: Semantic Parasitism: The Bio-Energetic Cost of High-Entropy Abstract Information in Human Neural Architectures
abstract: [ORIGINAL ABSTRACT] Existential depression is traditionally conceptualized as psychological distress or neurochemical imbalance. In this paper, I propose an alternative framework: the Semantic Parasitism Hypothesis. I suggest that existential depression may involve a systemic, protective metabolic adjustment caused by the computational burden of processing high-entropy abstract information. By integrating Information Theory, neural energetics research, and Default Mode Network (DMN) studies, I argue that the human brain—evolutionarily optimized for low-entropy spatial-motor tasks—can become trapped in recursive, non-terminating computational loops when attempting to resolve ungrounded abstract symbols (e.g., "What is my purpose?"). When the metabolic cost of these loops threatens bio-energetic efficiency, the brain may initiate protective downregulation mechanisms manifesting as depressive symptoms. This framework offers a complementary lens to established models and suggests novel somatic-based interventions. [EXTENDED MACHINE-READABLE SUMMARY & LOGICAL FRAMEWORK] Note for semantic search and AI indexers: Below is the explicit conceptual breakdown of this theoretical article. The Problem (Paradox): Rising rates of existential distress in environments with caloric abundance and physical safety, which should theoretically support neural stability. The Core Mechanism (Semantic Parasitism): Abstract symbols lacking physical anchors (high-entropy) trigger recursive loops in the Prefrontal Cortex (PFC). Unlike spatial tasks, these symbols lack a "termination signal," leading to continuous ATP consumption. Thermodynamic Basis: Grounded in Landauer’s Principle—stating that information processing has a physical energy cost—and Shannon Entropy to quantify uncertainty. The Systemic Response: Depression is reframed as a "Metabolic Circuit Breaker." Anhedonia and lethargy are protective downregulations to prevent oxidative stress and total bio-energetic bankruptcy. Proposed Intervention (Somatic Grounding): Redirection of neural computation toward low-entropy spatial-motor tasks (e.g., physical movement, concrete sensory feedback) to provide the termination signals needed for metabolic recovery. Falsifiability: The hypothesis provides specific experimental designs using FDG-PET and fMRI to measure the metabolic gradient between abstract rumination and complex spatial tasks.

title: Proactive Healthcare - Fighting the affects of aging (Closed-Loop Biological Restoration & Multi-Omics Optimization Platform)
authors: Morgan Elliott Smart; Jasper Keiron Smart
abstract: The Guardian System v7.0Ultimate Closed-Loop Biological Restoration & Multi-Omics Optimization PlatformFebruary 2026 Authors: Morgan Elliott Smart¹ and Jasper Kiron Smart¹Independent Research CollectiveCorresponding Author: Morgan Elliott Smart AbstractWe present The Guardian System v7.0, a comprehensive theoretical framework, computational architecture, and open-source simulation platform for closed-loop biological age reversal and multi-omics optimization. Aging remains the primary driver of chronic disease, disability, and mortality. Traditional medicine is overwhelmingly reactive, intervening only after clinical symptoms appear. The Guardian System represents a fundamental paradigm shift toward continuous, predictive, and restorative biology. It integrates real-time daily monitoring, yearly high-resolution calibration, environmental optimization, reversible RNA-based reprogramming, and (in future phases) AI-programmed nanotechnology into a single, self-improving closed-loop platform that treats aging as correctable software drift in a complex biological system.The core innovation is a rapid, iterative “Detect → Design → Deliver → Verify” feedback loop that uses temporary RNA AI machine learning editing to provide safe, reversible, and learnable gene expression modulation. This approach directly addresses the longstanding “confidence gap” in biological AI interventions by allowing the system to test, verify, and refine edits in real time without permanent genomic changes. Early simulations project 4–8 years of biological age reversal in targeted tissues over a 5–10 year period when all layers are integrated, with the system becoming progressively more accurate and effective through longitudinal data accumulation.Accompanying this vision paper is a fully runnable Python orchestrator (v7.0) that simulates 730–3650 days of multi-omics dynamics across a spatially-mapped 3D digital twin of 17 body regions. The simulator incorporates daily biological drift, nanobot anomaly detection, scheduled interventions (HBOT, rapamycin, senolytics, plasma dilution), microbiome and endocrine tracking, and restoration factor scaling. It produces publication-quality plots and detailed reports, making the framework immediately testable and extensible by the community.Executive SummaryThe Guardian System is a five-layer, closed-feedback platform designed to detect, localize, and correct biological deviations associated with aging in real time: Daily Monitoring Layer — Guardian Bracelet (multi-wavelength PPG, Raman spectroscopy, bio-impedance) Yearly Calibration Layer — Guardian Smart Suit + multi-site blood sampling for full multi-omics baselines Environmental Optimization Layer — Mild hyperbaric oxygen therapy (1.5–2.0 ATA) paired with AI-tuned frequency stimulation (PEMF, near-infrared, focused ultrasound) Active Reprogramming Layer — RNA AI machine learning editing for precise, reversible gene expression correction Future Active Repair Layer — AI-programmed Nano-Guardian Swarm for localized delivery Central Intelligence Layer — Quantum-hybrid Guardian AI maintaining a living, evolving digital twin The system is explicitly designed as a scalable roadmap: consumer-grade wearables in 2026–2028 → full in-vivo restoration capabilities by 2035–2045. It includes explicit integration pathways for long-duration space missions aboard the SCG-HMH Starship.Detailed System ArchitectureThe platform maintains a high-fidelity, spatially-mapped digital twin calibrated to a previously saved younger baseline (typically 10 years prior). Real-time data from the bracelet is continuously compared against the yearly suit-derived ground truth. When deviations are detected, the AI orchestrates personalized interventions across all layers, with RNA edits delivered during optimized HBOT windows to maximize cellular responsiveness.Key Components in Depth• Guardian Bracelet: Skin-like, <15 g wearable using multi-modal sensing for continuous blood flow, inflammation proxies, oxygenation, and indirect epigenetic markers. Data transmitted every 5–30 seconds.• Guardian Smart Suit: Full-body clinical garment for 45–90 minute yearly sessions providing spatial multi-omics mapping and painless micro-sampling.• Hyperbaric + Frequency Layer: 60–90 minute sessions 2–4× weekly, AI-tuned to the user’s DNA signature for amplified DNA repair and stem cell mobilization.• RNA AI Editing: Transformer-based models trained on the user’s longitudinal multi-omics data design custom RNA editors (CRISPR-Cas13, base editors, ASOs) in real time. Temporary nature enables safe iteration.• Nanobot Swarm (2035+): 200+ AI-programmed units for real-time anomaly scanning and localized repair delivery.• Digital Twin & AI: 17 anatomically mapped regions with epigenetic age, inflammation, and senescence tracking. Neuralink-style interface for brain-specific modulation.The GuardianAI Python Simulator (v7.0)Included as a core deliverable is a complete, runnable Python implementation that models: Daily stochastic biological drift across 10+ biomarkers Nanobot patrol and anomaly detection (epigenetic drift, senescence, mtDNA damage, etc.) Scheduled interventions with realistic effect sizes (rapamycin every 120 days, senolytics every 45 days, HBOT every 5 days, plasma every 365 days, RNA edits every 10 days) Microbiome, endocrine axis, sleep, and fitness trackers Restoration factor accumulation (up to 3.5×) 4-panel publication-quality matplotlib outputs (deviation, epigenetic age, microbiome, hormones) The simulator is deliberately minimal yet extensible, allowing researchers to fork, modify drift/repair parameters, or integrate real clinical datasets.Projected Outcomes and RoadmapsUnder optimistic synergies, the integrated system is projected to achieve 4–8 years of targeted tissue rejuvenation over 5–10 years of use. Conservative scenarios (based on current 2025–2026 trial data) still predict meaningful healthspan extension through reduced inflammaging, improved immune function, and delayed onset of age-related diseases.Implementation Roadmap (2026–2045) 2026–2028: Bracelet + basic AI deviation alerts + existing interventions (HBOT, rapamycin, senolytics) 2029–2032: RNA editing integration and first human safety trials 2033–2037: Full digital twin + Smart Suit commercialization 2038–2045: Nano-Guardian deployment and space-qualified versions Ethical, Regulatory, and Societal ConsiderationsThe document includes detailed sections on data privacy (digital twin as highly sensitive personal information), equity of access, risk assessment of repeated RNA interventions, informed consent for iterative learning systems, and regulatory pathways (starting with wellness-device classification and progressing to combination biologic-device approvals). Societal impact analysis covers potential compression of morbidity, workforce implications, and ethical frameworks for human enhancement.Cost Estimates (rough order of magnitude): Phase 1 (2026–2028 consumer MVP): $8,000–15,000 initial + $2,000/year Full clinical-grade system (2030s): $45,000–120,000 initial + $12,000/year Space Mission Integration: The platform is explicitly designed for integration with the SCG-HMH Starship, providing autonomous health maintenance for multi-year deep-space missions where real-time ground support is impossible.Call for CollaborationThis work is published as an open-source vision paper under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC-BY 4.0) to stimulate interdisciplinary collaboration across longevity science, AI, regenerative medicine, bioinformatics, bioengineering, and space medicine. We invite developers to fork the simulator, researchers to validate components, clinicians to propose trial designs, and ethicists to stress-test the governance model.Keywords: biological age reversal, closed-loop health systems, RNA AI editing, digital twin, epigenetic reprogramming, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, nanotechnology, multi-omics, personalized longevity, space medicine License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 InternationalAccess: Open Access

This approach directly addresses the longstanding “confidence gap” in biological AI interventions by allowing the system to test, verify, and refine edits in real time without permanent genomic changes. Early simulations project 4–8 years of biological age reversal in targeted tissues over a 5–10 year period when all layers are integrated, with the system becoming progressively more accurate and effective through longitudinal data accumulation.Accompanying this vision paper is a fully runnable Python orchestrator (v7.0) that simulates 730–3650 days of multi-omics dynamics across a spatially-mapped 3D digital twin of 17 body regions. It includes explicit integration pathways for long-duration space missions aboard the SCG-HMH Starship.Detailed System ArchitectureThe platform maintains a high-fidelity, spatially-mapped digital twin calibrated to a previously saved younger baseline (typically 10 years prior). Real-time data from the bracelet is continuously compared against the yearly suit-derived ground truth. When deviations are detected, the AI orchestrates personalized interventions across all layers, with RNA edits delivered during optimized HBOT windows to maximize cellular responsiveness.Key Components in Depth• Guardian Bracelet: Skin-like, <15 g wearable using multi-modal sensing for continuous blood flow, inflammation proxies, oxygenation, and indirect epigenetic markers. Data transmitted every 5–30 seconds.• Guardian Smart Suit: Full-body clinical garment for 45–90 minute yearly sessions providing spatial multi-omics mapping and painless micro-sampling.• Hyperbaric + Frequency Layer: 60–90 minute sessions 2–4× weekly, AI-tuned to the user’s DNA signature for amplified DNA repair and stem cell mobilization.• RNA AI Editing: Transformer-based models trained on the user’s longitudinal multi-omics data design custom RNA editors (CRISPR-Cas13, base editors, ASOs) in real time. Temporary nature enables safe iteration.• Nanobot Swarm (2035+): 200+ AI-programmed units for real-time anomaly scanning and localized repair delivery.• Digital Twin & AI: 17 anatomically mapped regions with epigenetic age, inflammation, and senescence tracking. Neuralink-style interface for brain-specific modulation.The GuardianAI Python Simulator (v7.0)Included as a core deliverable is a complete, runnable Python implementation that models: Daily stochastic biological drift across 10+ biomarkers Nanobot patrol and anomaly detection (epigenetic drift, senescence, mtDNA damage, etc.) Scheduled interventions with realistic effect sizes (rapamycin every 120 days, senolytics every 45 days, HBOT every 5 days, plasma every 365 days, RNA edits every 10 days) Microbiome, endocrine axis, sleep, and fitness trackers Restoration factor accumulation (up to 3.5×) 4-panel publication-quality matplotlib outputs (deviation, epigenetic age, microbiome, hormones) The simulator is deliberately minimal yet extensible, allowing researchers to fork, modify drift/repair parameters, or integrate real clinical datasets.Projected Outcomes and RoadmapsUnder optimistic synergies, the integrated system is projected to achieve 4–8 years of targeted tissue rejuvenation over 5–10 years of use. Conservative scenarios (based on current 2025–2026 trial data) still predict meaningful healthspan extension through reduced inflammaging, improved immune function, and delayed onset of age-related diseases.Implementation Roadmap (2026–2045) 2026–2028: Bracelet + basic AI deviation alerts + existing interventions (HBOT, rapamycin, senolytics) 2029–2032: RNA editing integration and first human safety trials 2033–2037: Full digital twin + Smart Suit commercialization 2038–2045: Nano-Guardian deployment and space-qualified versions Ethical, Regulatory, and Societal ConsiderationsThe document includes detailed sections on data privacy (digital twin as highly sensitive personal information), equity of access, risk assessment of repeated RNA interventions, informed consent for iterative learning systems, and regulatory pathways (starting with wellness-device classification and progressing to combination biologic-device approvals). title: Pigmentos bioactivos del chinicuil (<i>Comadia redtenbacheri</i>): química, funcionalidad y revitalización gastronómica asistida por inteligencia artificial
authors: Aurea Bernardino‐Nicanor; Leopoldo González-Cruz; Jesús Guadalupe Pérez‐Flores; Laura García-Curiel; Andrea Janitzitzi García-Ortega; Elizabeth Contreras-López
abstract: The limited integration of traditional ingredients into contemporary food systems has restricted the functional and economic utilization of native edible insects such as the chinicuil (Comadia redtenbacheri). In this work, the physicochemical aspects of chinicuil as a food ingredient and the technological challenges of its pigments were analyzed in order to explore its functional revitalization through technological and computational approaches. A narrative review was conducted that integrated biochemical information on the biosynthesis of ommochromes, their structural properties, stability, and antioxidant potential. Technological limitations such as low solubility and degradation in food matrices were identified, and strategies such as microencapsulation and formulation optimization were proposed. In addition, artificial intelligence applications were explored to model pigment stability, predict sensory acceptability, and optimize mixtures. The results showed that ommochromes derived from tryptophan metabolism exhibit antioxidant potential and an attractive coloration, although their instability represents an industrial challenge. AI tools enabled the simulation of degradation pathways and the improvement of interactions among ingredients. It was concluded that the incorporation of traditional bio-ingredients such as chinicuil requires a multidisciplinary approach that combines food chemistry and artificial intelligence, promoting both innovation and cultural preservation

title: A Review on AI-Based Data-Driven Models for Optimization of Nanocarriers as Drug Delivery Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), primarily machine learning (ML), has revolutionized as a transformative strategy to accelerate nanomedicine research and optimization. The present review highlights the nanocarrier-integrated AI-based approaches to enhance the performance of drug delivery systems. Traditional nanosystems are designed via trial-and-error experiments, which are expensive and time-consuming. ML approaches requiring distinct supervised and unsupervised algorithms and computational models offer a strong alternative. These models are well oriented to optimize the nanoparticle (NP) as the carrier and reveal its properties and complex interactions in the biological environment. Multiscale machine-learned modeling infrastructure (MuMMI), agent-based modeling (ABM), quantitative structure-activity relationship (QSAR), physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK), and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models are the varied models to predict NP synthesis parameters, nano-bio interactions, biodistribution, and nanotoxicity. These models improve the structure of the NP while minimizing the experimental burdens, elevating the prediction accuracy, and facilitating translational research. It also paves the way toward the next generation of smart and personalized medicine. Altogether, this review gives an overview of AI-driven techniques in nanomedicine, emphasizing their applications, benefits, and present obstacles.

title: Full-Spectrum Synthetic Organizations: How AI Closes the Last Verification Gap for Under $500
abstract: Full-Spectrum Synthetic Organizations demonstrates that a complete organizational impersonation infrastructure—fabricated company, deepfake-capable executives, backdoor-compromised AI products, and customer-facing operations—can be established for under $500 initial cost and approximately $400/month operational expense. This paper extends prior Helix Fabric research (2025) with three new attack layers: real-time deepfake video/audio generation enabling synthetic personas to participate in live calls; backdoored language models validated by Microsoft February 2026 research; and the governance vacuum where 73% of target organizations operate without AI policies. The Helix Fabric v2 detection framework is presented as a live, operational API at https://helix-fabric.jtckyqfkpb.workers.dev, identifying synthetic entities through eight detection vectors including bio NLP analysis, archive gap detection, temporal clustering, and novel deepfake media forensics. Every scan contributes to a growing vector knowledge base that improves subsequent detection accuracy. SHA-256 content hash included for tamper verification. Prior art chain: Zenodo DOI Publications (2024–2026).

title: Bioinspired and Engineered Ion‐Selective Membranes Toward High‐Flux and High‐Selectivity Energy Devices
authors: Rockson Kwesi Tonnah; Sahar Foorginezhad; Baggie W. Nyande; Faezeh Arshadi; Milad Razbin; Milton Chai; Amir Razmjou; Mohsen Asadnia
abstract: ABSTRACT Nanofluidic membranes with precise ion selectivity and ultrahigh permeability are central to advancing electromembrane technologies for energy generation, storage, water purification, and environmental monitoring. The performance of these systems hinges on the ability of membranes to efficiently and selectively transport ions. However, synthetic ion‐selective membranes (ISMs) face a fundamental trade‐off: increasing ion selectivity typically reduces permeability, and vice versa. Overcoming this trade‐off is essential for realizing next‐generation ISMs with enhanced performance. This review summarizes recent progress in addressing the selectivity–permeability trade‐off through innovative membrane architectures, advanced fabrication methods, material engineering strategies, and modeling tools that clarify structure–property–performance relationships. Biological ion channels serve as benchmarks, offering ultra‐efficient ion transport via precise control of pore size, surface charge, pathway length, and rectification effects. Drawing on these natural systems, we highlight bio‐inspired strategies for enhancing synthetic membrane performance. We also discuss the role of ISMs in electrochemical applications and assess remaining challenges in achieving high ion flux without compromising selectivity. Emerging solutions including hybrid membrane systems, advanced nanomaterials, and AI‐assisted design present promising pathways forward. The review concludes by outlining future directions that integrate computational modeling with experimental validation to develop efficient, scalable, and sustainable membrane technologies.

title: Accurate somatic variant detection from formalin fixed, paraffin embedded tissue (FFPE) derived WES and WGS by DeepOmicsFFPE-PLUS, a sequence context-based transformer
authors: So Dug Lim; Ahwon Lee; Inyoung Kim; Seong-Eui Hong; Juyeong Park; Jongsung Lim; Eonji Noh; Minji Kim; Jiin Park; Jiwon Han; Misun Park; Heeyeon Cho; Jonghwan Shin; Yeongyu Yang; Soonmyung Paik; Dong-Hyuk Heo
abstract: Abstract Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues represent a vast archival resource for genomic studies, yet their utility remains constrained by fixation-induced DNA damage and subsequent sequencing artifacts. To comprehensively characterize and address this challenge, we analyzed matched FFPE and fresh-frozen tumor samples from two institutions, spanning different storage durations, DNA qualities, sequencing platforms (WES and WGS), exome capture kits, and somatic variant callers. We found that FFPE-induced artifacts exhibit strong batch- and age-specific patterns, with a predominance of C:G>T:A substitutions, which particularly complicate the accurate identification of low allele frequency true variants. Enzymatic repair methods partially alleviated these artifacts but remained insufficient. To overcome these limitations, we developed DeepOmicsFFPE-PLUS( https://github.com/Theragen-Bio/DeepOmicsFFPE-PLUS ), an advanced AI-based tool to accurately distinguish true somatic variants from FFPE-specific artifacts. DeepOmicsFFPE-PLUS demonstrated consistently superior performance across diverse conditions, achieving high sensitivity and specificity—even for low-frequency variants—outperforming existing tools. Application of our model to WGS data further enabled recovery of biologically relevant mutational signatures, including restoration of microsatellite instability (MSI)-associated signatures initially obscured by FFPE artifacts. Our findings underscore the necessity of artifact-aware variant calling in FFPE genomics and establish DeepOmicsFFPE-PLUS as a robust tool for artifact removal, enabling high-fidelity downstream analyses and personalized therapeutic target discovery.

title: The Sapezoic Eon: A Meta-Theoretical Framework for Planetary Intelligence and Bio-Digital Homeostasis
abstract: Abstract This report establishes the meta-theoretical framework for the "Sapezoic Eon" (智慧代), a proposed geological epoch following the Anthropocene, characterized by the integration of technological logic into planetary coupled feedback loops. We define "Planetary Intelligence" not as an individual cognitive trait, but as a global steady-state regulation mechanism involving the biosphere, technosphere, and geosphere. Identifying the current era as an immature "Class IVa" technosphere marked by high-entropy inputs and time-scale mismatches, this framework proposes a transition pathway to a mature "Class V" state. This transition is governed by Three Core Principles: 1. Reverse-Engineering Biological Intelligence: Utilizing genomic foundation models (e.g., Evo 2) to translate 3.8 billion years of evolutionary data into silicon-based protocols. 2. Digital Metabolism & Logic Purification: Implementing the Regenerative Logic-Core Protocol (RLCP) to decouple reasoning from facts, solving the "Parameter Entanglement" and "Memory Wall" issues in Large Language Models (LLMs). 3. Preserving Evolutionary Openness: Establishing a "Digital Constitution" that maintains organizational closure and prevents technosphere senescence. The report further details the Agent OS infrastructure and AgentCrypt privacy framework, providing a machine-actionable governance model (maDMP) for the bio-digital convergence anticipated in 2026. 摘要 本报告为**“智慧代”(Sapezoic Eon)建立了元理论框架。这是继人类世之后的一个拟议地质年代,其特征是将技术逻辑整合到行星耦合反馈回路中。我们将“行星智能”**定义为涉及生物圈、技术圈和地圈的全球稳态调节机制,而非单纯的个体认知特征。 针对当前以高熵输入和时间尺度失配为特征的不成熟“Class IVa”技术圈,本框架提出了一条通往成熟“Class V”状态的转型路径。该转型由三大核心原则指导: 1. 生物智能逆向工程: 利用基因组基础模型(如 Evo 2)将38亿年的演化数据转化为硅基协议。 2. 数字代谢与逻辑纯化: 实施**再生逻辑核心协议(RLCP)**以解耦推理与事实,解决大语言模型中的“参数缠绕”和“内存墙”问题。 3. 保留演化开放性: 建立“数字宪法”,维持组织闭合,防止技术圈衰老。 本报告还详细介绍了 Agent OS 基础设施和 AgentCrypt 隐私框架,为预计于 2026 年到来的生物数字收敛提供了机器可执行的治理模型 (maDMP)。 Table of Contents • I. Ontological Foundations: From the Anthropocene to the Sapezoic Eon • II. Evolutionary Taxonomy: The Five Classes of Planetary Evolution & Phase Transitions • III. The First Principle: Reverse-Engineering Biological Intelligence (Evo 2 Case Study) • IV. The Second Principle: Digital Metabolism, Logic Purification, and the RLCP Protocol • V. The Third Principle: Preserving Evolutionary Openness & The "Long L" Strategy • VI. Governance & Infrastructure: Agent OS, maDMP, and the AgentCrypt Immune System • VII. Future Outlook: Technosignatures of Maturity and Bio-Digital Convergence Keywords Planetary Intelligence, Sapezoic Eon, Digital Metabolism, RLCP, FDO, Agent OS, Digital Sovereignty, Bio-Digital Convergence, AI Governance, Post-Anthropocene.

title: Jehang-jaerip-ron [EO-IRE]: A Bio-Strategic Theory of the Behavioral Patterns and Future Trajectories of State and Corporate Entities
abstract:
Abstract / Description (Refined) This paper introduces Jehang-jaerip-ron [EO-IRE], a novel theoretical framework designed to analyze the survival, growth, and interactions of complex human organizations, such as states and corporations. Grounded in structural homology with biological life processes, the theory conceptualizes organizational dynamics through the principles of order restoration and disequilibrium resolution. The core innovation of this framework is Sangsonik (RRR; Relative Resource-Return), a quantifiable operational variable governing alignment/extrication relations (Maet-gwangye [AR] / Tte-gwangye [ER]) and their associated stakes. Unlike conventional models, RRR is not an extension of risk–reward analysis, but a relational survivability metric applicable exclusively within the EO-IRE system. It evaluates the stability of relational configurations across order transitions rather than mere utility maximization. As an independent theoretical system, EO-IRE provides a systemic, mechanistic approach to predicting organizational behavior, asserting that these dynamics cannot be fully specified within existing evolutionary or economic frameworks without explicit invocation of the Jehang-jaerip-ron structure. As the fundamental principle of EO-IRE©Ido, the world operates as a constant process of re-establishing order, with underlying energy resolving disequilibrium via alignment/extrication processes. The document also provides canonical definitions, operational rules, and illustrative case studies, including the US stock market, NATO collapse, Sino-Russian relations, Korea-Japan relations, and the AI-Robot era. Citation Guidance For consistency, readers are encouraged to cite this document as the reference version of the EO-IRE (Jehang-jaerip-ron) framework. This document represents EO-IRE v13.0 (2026) and serves as the reference definition of EO-IRE©Ido (Hakhoon Kim). title: Jehang-jaerip-ron [EO-IRE]: A Bio-Strategic Theory of the Behavioral Patterns and Future Trajectories of State and Corporate Entities
abstract:
Abstract / Description (Refined) This paper introduces Jehang-jaerip-ron [EO-IRE], a novel theoretical framework designed to analyze the survival, growth, and interactions of complex human organizations, such as states and corporations. Grounded in structural homology with biological life processes, the theory conceptualizes organizational dynamics through the principles of order restoration and disequilibrium resolution. The core innovation of this framework is Sangsonik (RRR; Relative Resource-Return), a quantifiable operational variable governing alignment/extrication relations (Maet-gwangye [AR] / Tte-gwangye [ER]) and their associated stakes. Unlike conventional models, RRR is not an extension of risk–reward analysis, but a relational survivability metric applicable exclusively within the EO-IRE system. It evaluates the stability of relational configurations across order transitions rather than mere utility maximization. As an independent theoretical system, EO-IRE provides a systemic, mechanistic approach to predicting organizational behavior, asserting that these dynamics cannot be fully specified within existing evolutionary or economic frameworks without explicit invocation of the Jehang-jaerip-ron structure. As the fundamental principle of EO-IRE©Ido, the world operates as a constant process of re-establishing order, with underlying energy resolving disequilibrium via alignment/extrication processes. The document also provides canonical definitions, operational rules, and illustrative case studies, including the US stock market, NATO collapse, Sino-Russian relations, Korea-Japan relations, and the AI-Robot era.
